cohort: The study included 189 healthy singleton term born neonates, stratified by sex and gestation-specific body fat percentiles.
finding: Infants born with low body fatness had higher aortic intima-media thickness, lower heart rate variability, and thicker ventricular walls, while infants with high body fatness showed lower stroke volume and heart rate variability compared to those with average body fatness, indicating altered markers of cardiovascular health at both ends of the body fat spectrum.
